critiques.description: Mapping for req-WEBHOOK-001 treats satisfaction as merely unverified despite strong evidence that the callback endpoint lacks any origin authentication and processes unsigned requests from arbitrary callers as if they were from the payment provider.
critiques.rationale:
The mapping correctly marks req-WEBHOOK-001 as applicable and cites that inbound event authenticity is directly relevant to thr-001, but its satisfaction_status is "unverified" with a downgrade_reason referencing potential common false positives. That caution conflicts with the documented behaviour of the Callback Receiver and with the threat description built on it.

evd-002 states that the Callback Receiver "processes any well-formed callback it receives" and that callbacks are not signed and the provider’s optional signing feature is not enabled. evd-005 further documents that "the callback endpoint accepts unsigned requests from anywhere" and that "any caller that formats a callback correctly is processed as though it came from the payment provider." Taken together, these passages directly support the inference that there is no effective origin authentication beyond knowing the URL: any Internet client that can reach the endpoint and satisfy the schema is treated as the payment provider.

thr-001’s description and attack path (which the assessment has classified as supported based on evd-001–evd-003 and evd-005) depend on this behaviour to conclude that an external party can forge callbacks with arbitrary order identifiers and statuses that will be propagated into the operations channel. That scenario would not hold if a meaningful origin-binding control (such as provider-only network access, a shared secret, or another authenticated mechanism) were in place.

In this context, treating req-WEBHOOK-001 as merely "unverified" implies that the existence of sufficient authenticity controls remains an open question, even though evd-002 and evd-005 already document that any correctly formatted, unsigned callback from anywhere is processed as genuine. This creates a tension between the threat analysis (which relies on the absence of such controls and is marked supported) and the mapping’s downgraded satisfaction status. The mapping should either (a) acknowledge req-WEBHOOK-001 as unmet in light of this evidence, or (b) explicitly document any additional authenticity mechanism believed to satisfy the requirement, in which case thr-001 and its evidence assessment would need revisiting. As it stands, the combination of a high-confidence spoofing threat and an "unverified" status for the corresponding webhook-authenticity requirement is analytically inconsistent.
